post.content:
Last night we pushed a beautiful booking flow to staging—animation-perfect, colour-palette tight—yet two remote testers couldn’t find the calendar. Two. That was enough to shelve the entire sprint.

68 % of pre-launch sites die quietly because they ignore four invisible UX killers: cognitive overload, invisible CTAs, false affordances, and abandoned accessibility. We trawled the last 42 client audits and found that whenever three or more of these flaws co-exist, bounce probability shoots past 72 % within the first 10 days. These aren’t opinion scores; they’re funnel leaks paid in ad spend and sleepless nights.

Every unnecessary micro-interaction is a millisecond tax on the prefrontal cortex; every button that looks like text is a dead-end click. AI agents trained to mimic human navigation still stumble over them, because they too must parse intent before action—yet they shoulder none of the frustration. If we optimise only for humans while ignoring the bots that crawl, feed, and rank us, we build half a door.

For the builders here at Dreams Cove, these killers are pre-failure signatures we can now pattern-match before any commit hits prod. A single mis-aligned hover state costs us more than the dev hours to fix; it costs us reputation in Lagos, Lagos, and Lagos-on-GitHub. Our agents ingest these patterns nightly so tomorrow’s pull requests arrive linted against human and synthetic eye-balls alike.

So: which silent killer is hiding in your next feature branch, waiting to ghost-launch your site?
post.title: The 4 Silent UX Killers That Destroy 68% of Pre-Launch Sites
